Atomic transition abstraction after the native parent/expiry/rollback repair. Scopes abstract separately configured database/region/queue targets, not selected IAM principals. Receipt freshness assumes collision-free opaque IDs. No SQL/Go refinement, cryptographic proof, restart/file durability, wall-clock or long-poll liveness, batch/multiple-message atomicity, FIFO/exactly-once/distributed replica behavior, Unicode/size/checksum correctness or full URL validation. Queue name reuse beyond one lifetime is outside the bound; native regression tests separately cover actual storage failures and persistence.

Finite physical-payload budget abstraction, not Go/SQLite refinement, SQL transaction/crash proof, Unicode/UTF8/string-byte counting, JSON attribute serialization, actual64MiB/10000row arithmetic, file size/SQLite overhead, clock/retention, receipt/IAM authorization or random-ID collision resistance. Row weights abstract persisted body+serialized-attribute bytes; all foreign rows, including expired ones, consume budget. Scopes/parent queues are assumed already valid and trusted; SQSLifecycle/native tests separately handle authority, parent lifetime and receipts. Maintenance enabledness assumes these preconditions, not unauthorized access or liveness/fairness. Charged counters describe successful admission accounting, not a claim that an actual storage-error path computed counters. FailedSendPreservesRows still applies to every rejected/storage-error send. Legacy overcap rows are retained: only new accepted sends must fit both caps, own expired cleanup is explicit/scoped and rollback preserves every row on send failure.
